Caulfield

19/01/2007


Dear Dr. Isaacson,


Re: Mr. Jing ZU, aged 72


Thank you for seeing Mr. ZU, a retired school teacher, whose features are consistent with ischemic
heart disease. Your assessment and further management are highly appreciated.


Mr. ZU has had hypertension and ischemic heart disease for 18 years and 10 years, respectively. He
was diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction in 1999. Additionally, he has a history of congestive
cardiac failure for the past five years. He takes Lasix 40mg, enalapril 10mg, nifedipine 10mg and        Commented [OET1]: Do not use past period with the
Anginine as necessary.                                                                                   present simple tense. If you are going to do so please use
                                                                                                         the present perfect



Initially, Mr. ZU presented to me on 03/01/2007 complaining of exertional angina and mild postural
dizziness. His blood pressure was 160/90. His examination revealed bilateral basal crepitations in the
chest along with mild ankle edema. Therefore, he was diagnosed with stable congestive cardiac
failure and angina and watchful monitoring was recommended.


On 15/01/2007, Mr. ZU’s condition was further deteriorated with increased ankle edema,
crepitations in the chest and dyspnea along with orthopnea and elevated JVP. As a result, his dose
of Lasix was doubled and an ECG was advised.


Today, Mr. ZU’s dyspnea and chest crepitations has reduced. However, he reported an episode of           Commented [OET2]: have
exertional angina for ten minutes yesterday. His ECG has revealed anterolateral ischemic changes.


It would be greatly appreciated if you could further manage his condition. Please do not hesitate to
contact me if you have any queries.


Yours sincerely,
Doctor
